In contrast, when the bandwidth is higher (i.e., 64 or 128 Gbps), LMCACHE's loading consistently achieves lower delay than naive prefetching across all context lengths. These results suggest that LMCACHE's KV cache loading should be adaptive: under low bandwidth, loading should be enabled only when the context length surpasses the crossover point where loading becomes faster than prefetching. # 8.8 SGLang Results Although our primary evaluation uses vLLM, we also evaluate LMCACHE integrated with SGLang. Figure 16 reports results for Qwen3-32B served on two H100 GPUs (TP=2) with LMCACHE's CPU offloading enabled. Compared to SGLang without CPU offloading, LMCACHE achieves higher throughput and lower mean TTFT and mean end-to-end latency. Compared to SGLang's native CPU offloading, LMCACHE achieves comparable performance. These results confirm that LMCACHE is also effective on another inference engine. \widetilde {\mathrm {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) = \left[ \operatorname {S o f t m a x} (\mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} / \sqrt {d}) \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i}) \right] _ {i} \mathbf {W} ^ {O},
$$

where  $\widetilde{\mathrm{MHA}} (\mathbf{X}),\widetilde{\mathbf{K}}_i$  and  $\widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_i$  represent the approximation of MHA(X),  $\mathbf{K}_i$  and  $\mathbf{V}_i$  , respectively. The difference between the actual attention output and the one produced with approximate keys and values is upper bounded as

$$
\begin{array}{l} \| \widetilde {\operatorname {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) - \operatorname {M H A} (\mathbf {X}) \| _ {2} \\ \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {h} \frac {\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \| _ {2}}{\sqrt {d}} \| \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \mathbf {K} _ {i} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} \| _ {2} \\ + \left\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} - \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \right\| _ {2}. \tag {1} \\ \end{array}
$$

The method proposed by this paper stems from the will to minimize this upper bound on the output approximation error. In each attention head, for a key cache  $\mathbf{K}$  and a calibration set of query vectors  $\{\mathbf{q}^{(j)}\}_{j\in \mathrm{calibration}}$  (row vectors of size  $d$ ), we want to minimize

$$
\sum_ {j \in \text {c a l i b r a t i o n}} \| \mathbf {q} ^ {(j)} \mathbf {K} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {q} ^ {(j)} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} ^ {\top} \| _ {2} ^ {2},
$$

over low-rank  $\widetilde{\mathbf{K}}$ . This objective is equivalent to a low-rank approximation of the query-key interaction matrix and admits an optimal closed-form solution via the singular value decomposition. Similarly, to compress values we directly optimize the second term of Eq. (3) over low-rank  $\widetilde{\mathbf{V}}$  for each attention head (see Appendix B).

# 4.2 Proposed Method

In the following, we drop the head index  $i$  for ease of clarity. Our method addresses cache compression by producing an optimal solution to

$$
\min  _ {\widetilde {\mathbf {K}}} \| \mathbf {Q} \mathbf {K} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {Q} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} ^ {2} \text {s . t .} \operatorname {r a n k} (\widetilde {\mathbf {K}}) \leq R,
$$

with  $\mathbf{Q} = \left(\mathbf{q}^{(j)}\right)_{j\in \mathrm{calibration}}$  the collection of query vectors from the calibration set. This formulation jointly considers the properties of both  $\mathbf{K}$  and  $\mathbf{Q}$ , while taking into account their interaction through the inner product. The optimization problem can be restated using a projection matrix as

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {S}} \left\| \mathbf {K S Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \right\| _ {F} ^ {2} \quad \text {s . t .} \operatorname {r a n k} (\mathbf {S}) \leq R,
$$

where  $\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ . To be able to compress the key cache during the attention computation, we write the projection matrix  $\mathbf{S}$  as a product of two matrices, i.e.,  $\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B}$  with  $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times R}$ . The minimization problem tackled by KQ-SVD is thus

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} ^ {2}. \tag {2}
$$

Given  $\mathbf{A}^*$  and  $\mathbf{B}^*$  the solutions of this optimization problem, we store the low-rank matrix  $\mathbf{K}\mathbf{A}^{*}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ , which

allows for compression while maintaining an accurate reconstruction of the attention matrix. The same strategy also applies to the value-output matrices (see Appendix B). In the next section, we state the main theorem which demonstrates that the optimization problem described above admits an optimal solution which can be computed efficiently.

# 4.3 KQ-SVD: Optimal attention factorization

The following theorem establishes the provably optimal low-rank factorization of the key-query matrix, which admits a simple closed-form solution.

Theorem 2. Let  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  be key and query cache matrices. The optimal solution to the low rank attention approximation problem

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

is given by

$$
\mathbf {A} = \mathbf {K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}}, \mathbf {B} = \mathbf {K} ^ {T} \hat {\mathbf {U}},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$  is the matrix having the top  $R$  left singular vectors of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  as columns.

Proof. Observe that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}$  has rank at most  $R$ . Hence,

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

is lower bounded by

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {M} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {T \times T}} \| \mathbf {M} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} \text {s . t . r a n k} (\mathbf {M}) \leq R.
$$

By the Eckart-Young theorem, we know the best rank  $R$  approximation of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is given by its truncated SVD:

$$
\mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \simeq \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R},\hat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}\in \mathbb{R}^{R\times R}$  and  $\hat{\mathbf{V}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ . We will show that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}\hat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\hat{\mathbf{V}}^{\top}$  from which the optimality of  $\mathbf{A}$  and  $\mathbf{B}$  follows.

Let  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}\pmb{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}$  be the full SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$ . Observe that we have the inclusion of (column) spans:  $\mathcal{R}(\hat{\mathbf{U}})\subseteq \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{U}) = \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ . Since  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}$  is the orthogonal projection onto  $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ , we have  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}$ , hence

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} = \mathbf {K K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \\ = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {U} \boldsymbol {\Sigma} \mathbf {V} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top}. \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore  $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{K}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  and  $\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{K}^{\top}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  are optimal solutions to  $\min_{\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times R}}\| \mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} - \mathbf{KQ}^{\top}\|_{F}$ .

The Moore-Penrose pseudo inverse of  $\mathbf{K}$  can be expressed through the SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$  as  $\mathbf{K}^{+} = \mathbf{V}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}^{-1}\mathbf{U}_{K}^{\top}$ . The singular value decomposition of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times T}$  can be computed efficiently as its rank is at most  $d$ . Indeed, we can first perform an SVD on  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}$  and  $\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{U}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q}\mathbf{V}_{Q}^{\top}$ , then on the  $d \times d$  matrix  $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{V}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q} = \mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'\mathbf{V}'^{\top}$ . The SVD of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is then  $\mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'(\mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}')^{\top} = \mathbf{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^{\top}$  with  $\mathbf{U} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  and  $\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$ . This way the optimal solution provided by Theorem 2 can be computed efficiently in time  $\mathcal{O}(Td^{2})$ .

The method views the key and query matrices as a single entity and applies singular value decomposition (SVD) to  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$ . # 4.1 Motivation

Existing compression methods based on SVD typically compress keys or jointly embed  $\mathbf{Q} / \mathbf{K} / \mathbf{V}$ . Theorem 1 (proof in Appendix A) inspired by [Wang et al., 2025] shows why that can fail: perturbations in  $\mathbf{K}$  are amplified by the inner products  $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}$  and further propagated by the value multiplication.

Theorem 1. Let  $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  be a sequence of token embeddings,  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  and

$$
\mathrm {M H A} (\mathbf {X}) = \left[ \mathrm {S o f t m a x} (\mathbf {Q} _ {i} \mathbf {K} _ {i} ^ {\top} / \sqrt {d}) \mathbf {V} _ {i}) \right] _ {i} \mathbf {W} ^ {O},
$$

$$
\widetilde {\mathrm {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) = \left[ \operatorname {S o f t m a x} (\mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} / \sqrt {d}) \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i}) \right] _ {i} \mathbf {W} ^ {O},

The difference between the actual attention output and the one produced with approximate keys and values is upper bounded as

$$
\begin{array}{l} \| \widetilde {\operatorname {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) - \operatorname {M H A} (\mathbf {X}) \| _ {2} \\ \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {h} \frac {\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \| _ {2}}{\sqrt {d}} \| \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \mathbf {K} _ {i} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} \| _ {2} \\ + \left\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} - \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \right\| _ {2}. \tag {1} \\ \end{array}
$$

with  $\mathbf{Q} = \left(\mathbf{q}^{(j)}\right)_{j\in \mathrm{calibration}}$  the collection of query vectors from the calibration set. This formulation jointly considers the properties of both  $\mathbf{K}$  and  $\mathbf{Q}$ , while taking into account their interaction through the inner product. The optimization problem can be restated using a projection matrix as

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {S}} \left\| \mathbf {K S Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \right\| _ {F} ^ {2} \quad \text {s . t .} \operatorname {r a n k} (\mathbf {S}) \leq R,
$$

where  $\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ . To be able to compress the key cache during the attention computation, we write the projection matrix  $\mathbf{S}$  as a product of two matrices, i.e.,  $\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B}$  with  $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times R}$ . The minimization problem tackled by KQ-SVD is thus

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} ^ {2}. \tag {2}
$$

Given  $\mathbf{A}^*$  and  $\mathbf{B}^*$  the solutions of this optimization problem, we store the low-rank matrix  $\mathbf{K}\mathbf{A}^{*}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ , which

allows for compression while maintaining an accurate reconstruction of the attention matrix. The same strategy also applies to the value-output matrices (see Appendix B). In the next section, we state the main theorem which demonstrates that the optimization problem described above admits an optimal solution which can be computed efficiently.

# 4.3 KQ-SVD: Optimal attention factorization

The following theorem establishes the provably optimal low-rank factorization of the key-query matrix, which admits a simple closed-form solution.

Theorem 2. Let  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  be key and query cache matrices. The optimal solution to the low rank attention approximation problem

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

is given by

$$
\mathbf {A} = \mathbf {K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}}, \mathbf {B} = \mathbf {K} ^ {T} \hat {\mathbf {U}},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$  is the matrix having the top  $R$  left singular vectors of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  as columns.

Proof. Observe that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}$  has rank at most  $R$ . Hence,

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {M} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {T \times T}} \| \mathbf {M} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} \text {s . t . r a n k} (\mathbf {M}) \leq R.
$$

By the Eckart-Young theorem, we know the best rank  $R$  approximation of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is given by its truncated SVD:

$$
\mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \simeq \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R},\hat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}\in \mathbb{R}^{R\times R}$  and  $\hat{\mathbf{V}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ . We will show that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}\hat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\hat{\mathbf{V}}^{\top}$  from which the optimality of  $\mathbf{A}$  and  $\mathbf{B}$  follows.

Let  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}\pmb{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}$  be the full SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$ . Observe that we have the inclusion of (column) spans:  $\mathcal{R}(\hat{\mathbf{U}})\subseteq \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{U}) = \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ . Since  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}$  is the orthogonal projection onto  $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ , we have  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}$ , hence

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} = \mathbf {K K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \\ = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {U} \boldsymbol {\Sigma} \mathbf {V} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top}. \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore  $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{K}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  and  $\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{K}^{\top}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  are optimal solutions to  $\min_{\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times R}}\| \mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} - \mathbf{KQ}^{\top}\|_{F}$ .

The Moore-Penrose pseudo inverse of  $\mathbf{K}$  can be expressed through the SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$  as  $\mathbf{K}^{+} = \mathbf{V}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}^{-1}\mathbf{U}_{K}^{\top}$ . The singular value decomposition of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times T}$  can be computed efficiently as its rank is at most  $d$ . Indeed, we can first perform an SVD on  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}$  and  $\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{U}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q}\mathbf{V}_{Q}^{\top}$ , then on the  $d \times d$  matrix  $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{V}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q} = \mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'\mathbf{V}'^{\top}$ . The SVD of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is then  $\mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'(\mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}')^{\top} = \mathbf{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^{\top}$  with  $\mathbf{U} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  and  $\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$ . This way the optimal solution provided by Theorem 2 can be computed efficiently in time  $\mathcal{O}(Td^{2})$ .

# 6.1 Comparing methods

Setup: To validate our theoretical claims, we run experiments on several widely used LLMs. We test two models without grouped-query attention (GQA)—Llama2-7B and Llama2-13B [Touvron et al., 2023]—and two models with GQA—Llama3-8B [Grattafori et al., 2024] and Mistral7B-v0.3 [Jiang et al., 2023]. All experiments use the C4 dataset [Raffel et al., 2020], with projections learned on the training split and evaluated on the validation split.

Learning projections: Following the methodology of Saxena et al. [2024], we select 128 training sequences of 2048 tokens each from C4. Each sequence is passed through the model, storing the key, value, and query caches for every layer and attention head (queries are needed by both Eigen and KQ-SVD). For each layer-head pair, we collect the corresponding caches from all 128 sequences and concatenate them, yielding large matrices  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{T_{\mathrm{huge}} \times d}$  with  $T_{\mathrm{huge}} = 262,144$ . Because model context length is limited and attention cost scales quadratically with sequence length, it is not feasible to build these matrices from a single long sequence. Instead, we construct them from multiple shorter ones. Once the large cache matrices are formed, we perform SVD and apply the formulas presented in previous sections to compute low-rank projections.

Rank selection: All methods are evaluated at the same rank  $R$ , determined individually for each layer. For a given layer, we analyze the singular value spectra of the key and value matrices, averaged across heads, and choose the smallest  $R$  that discards no more than an  $\epsilon = 0.1$  fraction of the spectral energy. That is, for singular values  $\{\sigma_j\}_j$  of  $\mathbf{K}$ ,  $\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{R} \sigma_j^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{d} \sigma_j^2} \geq 1 - \epsilon$ . This is equivalent to requiring that the relative Frobenius error is at most  $\epsilon$ .

Evaluation: We evaluate the learned projections on 32 validation sequences of 2048 tokens each. For every sequence, we extract the cache matrices  $(\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V})$  at each layer and head. Using these matrices, we can simulate attention computations directly, since attention depends only on these three components. Each cache is projected onto its corresponding low-rank subspace to form approximations, and we then compute the approximate Multi-Head Attention output using the standard formulas. For comparison, we also compute the exact (uncompressed) attention output. This enables us to measure the relative error of each method across all matrices of the attention pipeline. Errors are averaged across validation sequences.

Metrics: For a matrix  $\mathbf{M}$  and its approximation  $\widetilde{\mathbf{M}}$ , we report the relative Frobenius norm error  $\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{Fro}} = \frac{\|\mathbf{M} - \widetilde{\mathbf{M}}\|_F^2}{\|\mathbf{M}\|_F^2}$ . This error is computed for the key, query, and value matrices, for the attention score matrix  $\mathbf{KQ}^\top$ , and for the Multi-Head Attention output MHA(X).

Results: Results are shown in Figure 1. For each model, the top plot reports the relative error on the attention output across layers, while the bottom plot reports the averaged errors on the intermediate components. We observe that K-SVD provides the most accurate approximation of the key matrices (as expected from the optimality of SVD), but performs poorly on query matrices, leading to weaker approximations of the attention scores and consequently

![](images/2512.05916/22e7e739f4f5f639947d4bf668484ee23791282e2cac3d75f5adaadf89856c4f.jpg)  
Figure 1: Relative Frobenius approximation output error per layer (top) and mean relative errors on  $\mathbf{K}$ ,  $\mathbf{Q}$ ,  $\mathbf{V}$ ,  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  and attention layer output across layers (bottom) for Mistral and Llama models.

higher output errors. This effect is more pronounced in GQA models, where sharing the key matrix across queries in a group amplifies approximation errors.

In contrast, Eigen and KQ-SVD achieve comparable accuracy on keys, queries, and values. The key difference lies in the attention score matrix: KQ-SVD consistently delivers higher accuracy, resulting in lower attention errors and outperforming all other methods on all models.

# 6.2 Unbalanced K and Q matrices

We verify experimentally the claims of Section 5.2 and analyze the attention approximation error under unbalanced  $\mathbf{K}$  and  $\mathbf{Q}$  matrices.

Set up: We follow the same experimental setup as in the previous section using the C4 train/validation split to learn projections and evaluate their accuracy. The only difference is that cache matrices are scaled to assess the effect of unbalance. Key matrices are multiplied by  $\beta$  and query matrices are divided by  $\beta$ . This is equivalent to scaling the projection matrices  $\mathbf{W}_{K,i} / \mathbf{W}_{Q,i}$  by  $\beta$ , as the operation permutes with matrix multiplication (this does not change the output since the query and key matrices are multiplied before any non-linear activation).

Metrics: For each unbalance ratio, we plot the relative attention output error for the three methods, averaged across all layers and validation sequences.

Results: Results are shown in Figure 2. As discussed in Section 5.2, K-SVD and KQ-SVD are invariant to scaling  $\mathbf{K}$  by a factor  $\beta$  and dividing  $\mathbf{Q}$  by the same factor, which is confirmed by the constant error observed for these methods. As predicted theoretically, a higher unbalance ratio brings Eigen closer to K-SVD; for  $\beta = 10$ , their errors are nearly indistinguishable. This confirms Theorem 4

![](images/2512.05916/2a45faceff8abb7f0552950d8abfa8409bd9b68859eb66de40962dafd2610db1.jpg)

{"command": "read-source", "ok": true, "result": {"source_content": {"content": "The theoretical results established in the previous sections require further validation on real cache matrices generated by state-of-the-art LLMs. In this section, we first compare KQ-SVD with K-SVD and Eigen, and then demonstrate the claim of Theorem 4 using real-world cache data.

# 6.1 Comparing methods

Setup: To validate our theoretical claims, we run experiments on several widely used LLMs. We test two models without grouped-query attention (GQA)—Llama2-7B and Llama2-13B [Touvron et al., 2023]—and two models with GQA—Llama3-8B [Grattafori et al., 2024] and Mistral7B-v0.3 [Jiang et al., 2023]. All experiments use the C4 dataset [Raffel et al., 2020], with projections learned on the training split and evaluated on the validation split.

Learning projections: Following the methodology of Saxena et al. [2024], we select 128 training sequences of 2048 tokens each from C4. Each sequence is passed through the model, storing the key, value, and query caches for every layer and attention head (queries are needed by both Eigen and KQ-SVD). For each layer-head pair, we collect the corresponding caches from all 128 sequences and concatenate them, yielding large matrices  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{T_{\mathrm{huge}} \times d}$  with  $T_{\mathrm{huge}} = 262,144$ . Because model context length is limited and attention cost scales quadratically with sequence length, it is not feasible to build these matrices from a single long sequence. Instead, we construct them from multiple shorter ones. Once the large cache matrices are formed, we perform SVD and apply the formulas presented in previous sections to compute low-rank projections.

Rank selection: All methods are evaluated at the same rank  $R$ , determined individually for each layer. For a given layer, we analyze the singular value spectra of the key and value matrices, averaged across heads, and choose the smallest  $R$  that discards no more than an  $\epsilon = 0.1$  fraction of the spectral energy. That is, for singular values  $\{\sigma_j\}_j$  of  $\mathbf{K}$ ,  $\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{R} \sigma_j^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{d} \sigma_j^2} \geq 1 - \epsilon$ . This is equivalent to requiring that the relative Frobenius error is at most  $\epsilon$ .

Evaluation: We evaluate the learned projections on 32 validation sequences of 2048 tokens each. For every sequence, we extract the cache matrices  $(\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V})$  at each layer and head. Using these matrices, we can simulate attention computations directly, since attention depends only on these three components. Each cache is projected onto its corresponding low-rank subspace to form approximations, and we then compute the approximate Multi-Head Attention output using the standard formulas. For comparison, we also compute the exact (uncompressed) attention output. This enables us to measure the relative error of each method across all matrices of the attention pipeline. Errors are averaged across validation sequences.

Metrics: For a matrix  $\mathbf{M}$  and its approximation  $\widetilde{\mathbf{M}}$ , we report the relative Frobenius norm error  $\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{Fro}} = \frac{\|\mathbf{M} - \widetilde{\mathbf{M}}\|_F^2}{\|\mathbf{M}\|_F^2}$ . This error is computed for the key, query, and value matrices, for the attention score matrix  $\mathbf{KQ}^\top$ , and for the Multi-Head Attention output MHA(X).

Results: Results are shown in Figure 1. For each model, the top plot reports the relative error on the attention output across layers, while the bottom plot reports the averaged errors on the intermediate components. We observe that K-SVD provides the most accurate approximation of the key matrices (as expected from the optimality of SVD), but performs poorly on query matrices, leading to weaker approximations of the attention scores and consequently

![](images/2512.05916/22e7e739f4f5f639947d4bf668484ee23791282e2cac3d75f5adaadf89856c4f.jpg)  
Figure 1: Relative Frobenius approximation output error per layer (top) and mean relative errors on  $\mathbf{K}$ ,  $\mathbf{Q}$ ,  $\mathbf{V}$ ,  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  and attention layer output across layers (bottom) for Mistral and Llama models.

higher output errors. This effect is more pronounced in GQA models, where sharing the key matrix across queries in a group amplifies approximation errors.

In contrast, Eigen and KQ-SVD achieve comparable accuracy on keys, queries, and values. The key difference lies in the attention score matrix: KQ-SVD consistently delivers higher accuracy, resulting in lower attention errors and outperforming all other methods on all models.

# 6.2 Unbalanced K and Q matrices

We verify experimentally the claims of Section 5.2 and analyze the attention approximation error under unbalanced  $\mathbf{K}$  and  $\mathbf{Q}$  matrices.

Set up: We follow the same experimental setup as in the previous section using the C4 train/validation split to learn projections and evaluate their accuracy. The only difference is that cache matrices are scaled to assess the effect of unbalance. Key matrices are multiplied by  $\beta$  and query matrices are divided by  $\beta$ . This is equivalent to scaling the projection matrices  $\mathbf{W}_{K,i} / \mathbf{W}_{Q,i}$  by  $\beta$ , as the operation permutes with matrix multiplication (this does not change the output since the query and key matrices are multiplied before any non-linear activation).

Metrics: For each unbalance ratio, we plot the relative attention output error for the three methods, averaged across all layers and validation sequences.

Results: Results are shown in Figure 2. As discussed in Section 5.2, K-SVD and KQ-SVD are invariant to scaling  $\mathbf{K}$  by a factor  $\beta$  and dividing  $\mathbf{Q}$  by the same factor, which is confirmed by the constant error observed for these methods. As predicted theoretically, a higher unbalance ratio brings Eigen closer to K-SVD; for  $\beta = 10$ , their errors are nearly indistinguishable. This confirms Theorem 4

![](images/2512.05916/2a45faceff8abb7f0552950d8abfa8409bd9b68859eb66de40962dafd2610db1.jpg)  
Figure 2: Llama2-7B relative output approximation error averaged across layers for varying unbalanced factor  $\beta$ .

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: c:\Users\wushuhong\Desktop\literature-research-clean-e2e-20260810-195219\.claude\skills\literature-research

# Literature Research

Use this skill when the user asks for an academic literature review, technical-route
survey, state-of-the-art analysis, research landscape, or evidence-backed technical
report. Claude is the semantic Researcher; the Python Harness is the deterministic
runtime for authority, persistence, stable references, provenance, accounting, and
validation.

Never edit `state.json`, event logs, report artifacts, or repository files directly.
All authoritative mutations must go through the Python harness entrypoint; host Web
observations remain ephemeral until promoted with `retain-papers`.

## Harness entrypoint

Invoke the harness through its single Python entrypoint. Resolve the installed
Skill directory, then run `scripts/harness.py` with the available Python
interpreter:

```text
python "<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/harness.py" --workspace PATH COMMAND [OPTIONS]
```

`harness.py` resolves the bundled Runtime itself and, if a Skill-local `.venv`
exists (created by `python scripts/setup.py`), switches to that interpreter
automatically before executing the command. The caller never needs to know the
venv interpreter path. `CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR` is an optional override of the Skill
root; otherwise `harness.py` resolves it from its own location. On Windows
PowerShell, Linux, and macOS the same command works; if the host exposes Python
as `py` rather than `python`, use that interpreter. See `RUNTIME_API.md` for the
command schemas.

## Read the protocol before acting

Read only the supporting material needed for the current stage:

- [Research protocol](references/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md): contracts, adaptive search,
  source reading, synthesis, recovery, and the outer loop.
- [Runtime API](references/RUNTIME_API.md): commands, JSON input shapes, revision
  handling, and error behavior.
- [Completion guide](references/COMPLETION_GUIDE.md): the independent completion
  boundary and PASS / CONTINUE / UNCERTAIN criteria.
- [Report writing guide](references/REPORT_WRITING_GUIDE.md): the authoritative style
  and editorial standard used by all semantic writing stages.
- [Research integrity guide](references/RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_GUIDE.md): evidence-strength,
  benchmark, comparison, causality, recency, and high-risk claim checks used by the
  independent Research Integrity Reviewer.

## Start from the request

Treat `调研 LLM KV Cache 优化的主要技术路线和最新进展，要求2025-2026年以内的，并且包含2026年最新的。请你深入分析一下` as the user's research request. If it is empty, ask for the topic,
intended audience, scope, and desired deliverable. Otherwise infer a conservative
initial Research Contract and state the important assumptions before creating it.

Convert the request into:

1. a precise mission;
2. independently checkable requirements;
3. an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope boundary;
4. a deliverable description;
5. required artifacts, normally `REPORT` for a written survey.

Do not encode fixed paper counts as completion conditions. Workload expectations can
guide exploration, but coverage, evidence quality, recency, contradiction handling,
and requirement satisfaction determine completion.

Run the environment check first:

```text
python "<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/harness.py" --workspace workspace doctor
```

Create a run using a JSON file, not shell-escaped inline JSON:

```text
python "<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/harness.py" --workspace workspace create-run \
  --input /tmp/research-contract.json
```

Keep runtime data in the chosen workspace, never inside the skill directory.

## Own the semantic outer loop

The Harness does not prescribe a fixed research finite-state machine. Claude owns an
adaptive outer loop:

```text
view current state
→ identify the highest-value uncertainty or gap
→ search, inspect, or read evidence for that uncertainty
→ retain selected papers and synthesize durable research objects
→ reassess coverage and contradictions against updated State
→ repeat, request completion, or explain a blocker
```

Each turn of this loop is one research iteration: it starts from a specific uncertainty,
acquires evidence for it, and updates State before the next turn. Do not run the loop as
a pipeline where a discovery phase feeds a fixed analysis phase. Choose the next action
from the reassessed State, not from the previous step's momentum.

After every state-changing command, use the returned `state_revision` for the next
command. On a revision conflict, discard the stale plan, call `view`, and reason again.

## Keep discovery inside the research loop

A search call is not a research iteration. For deep research, do not finish a broad
discovery batch before beginning source reading and synthesis. After each meaningful
evidence cluster: integrate durable State, reassess current uncertainty, and let that
updated State choose the next search or read action. Discovery, Primary Source reading,
synthesis, and reassessment should interleave throughout the run.

The failure mode to avoid is staged batching: search a broad batch → retain all → batch
analysis → one synthesis → request completion. That collapses the adaptive outer loop
into a pipeline and lets volume substitute for judgment. A broad discovery sweep may
contain multiple search calls inside one research iteration, but it must end by returning
to State reassessment, not by proceeding to a fixed analysis stage.

## Search through independent discovery channels

Use DeepXiv through `search-papers` first. It remains the primary scholarly semantic
search, pagination, source inspection, and targeted reading path. Begin broadly, learn
canonical routes and terminology, then expand by mechanism and explicit date windows.

Use Claude Code native `WebSearch` as an independent frontier counter-recall channel,
not a second authoritative paper database. For explicit latest/current/recent/SOTA
requests, always perform at least one Web frontier counter-search in addition to a
DeepXiv recent sweep. Also use it when retained recency is suspiciously stale, recent
terminology shifts, or a known paper is missing from DeepXiv results.

```text
foundation and route discovery → DeepXiv recent sweep → emerging-term expansion
→ native WebSearch counter-search → WebFetch canonical scholarly page
→ retain selected identity → Harness source verification → gap-driven follow-up
```

Keep this adaptive. Generate Web queries from actual methods, algorithms, rewards,
benchmarks, mechanisms, authors, and emerging terms; use `site:arxiv.org` or
`site:openreview.net` when useful. Prefer native `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`; never call
search engines through Bash or custom APIs.

```text
python "<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/harness.py" --workspace workspace search-papers \
  --run-id RUN --expected-revision REV --query "QUERY" \
  --limit 20 --offset 0 --date-from YYYY-MM-DD --date-to YYYY-MM-DD
```

Search output includes provider-reported `total_count`, and hits include publication
date as well as year when available. Use `total_count`, new unique identities, route
novelty, and recent-paper novelty to decide whether to page; do not mechanically exhaust
all results. A first page is discovery input, not proof of coverage, and local date
sorting of retrieved candidates is not a global latest-paper search.

DeepXiv hits, WebSearch results/snippets, and WebFetch pages are observations, not
evidence. Use WebSearch to find scholarly URLs and `WebFetch` to verify canonical
metadata. Follow blogs, labs, repositories, or news to an arXiv, OpenReview, DOI, or
publisher paper page; never retain the lead or fabricate an unconfirmed field.

Promote an important Web-discovered candidate with the existing `retain-papers` input,
using only verified metadata. Then use `inspect-source` and `read-source` before formal
analysis or claims; WebFetch does not bypass evidence access. If DeepXiv cannot inspect a
retained Web-only paper, record a source coverage gap rather than inventing a fallback.

## Inspect before reading

For a retained paper, call `inspect-source` first to obtain provider-supported sections.
Then call `read-source` with a targeted locator for methods, experiments, limitations,
or another specific need. Read the full source only when the structure is unavailable
or broad context is genuinely necessary.

This is the Primary Evidence Gate: a `PaperAnalysis` with mechanism-level claims,
empirical results, or detailed comparisons must rest on `inspect-source` /
`read-source` evidence, not on the abstract or search metadata that selected the
paper. A paper may be retained on abstract alone, but its detailed analysis may not
be written from the abstract. If primary-source access fails, record a source coverage
gap rather than manufacturing analysis from discovery metadata. `SourceContent` is
ephemeral; convert the evidence that matters into a concise `PaperAnalysis` with
useful `key_locators`, leaving them empty when no targeted locator applies.

## Synthesize periodically

Synthesis is part of each research iteration, not a final stage. After each meaningful
cluster of reading, update the structured landscape before choosing the next action:

- `PaperAnalysis` records what a retained paper contributes, shows, and fails to show.
- `ApproachFamily` groups methods sharing a real mechanism, not merely vocabulary.
- `Finding` records a supported cross-paper technical judgment.
- `OpenProblem` records an unresolved field-level question supported by the landscape.
- `InvestigationGap` records work still required for this run or contract.

An Open Problem belongs to the researched domain. A Gap belongs to the current research
process. Do not substitute one for the other.

Use source relations (`SUPPORTS`, `CHALLENGES`, `QUALIFIES`) and locators to preserve
evidence boundaries. Retire or update obsolete semantic objects through explicit
commands instead of silently changing their meaning.

For a deep technical-route survey, normally seek multiple query formulations, more
than one representative method per major route where the literature permits it,
seminal and frontier evidence, competing results, deployment conditions, and explicit
unknowns. These are exploration heuristics, never mechanical completion thresholds.

For an explicitly deep or comprehensive technical-route survey, a corpus of only a
few investigated papers is normally insufficient unless the scope is genuinely narrow.
Tens of deduplicated search candidates across multiple adaptive searches are a normal
exploration scale for a broad field survey. Before requesting Completion from a much
smaller corpus, the Researcher must be able to explain from the Contract and current
landscape why the scope is narrow enough that additional search is unlikely to reveal
a major route, representative method, disagreement, or recent frontier development.
This is workload guidance, not a paper-count or Completion threshold.

Before requesting Completion for a latest/recent task, answer from the retained corpus:
the newest relevant paper date, the searched recent window, the frontier queries used,
whether emerging terminology triggered follow-up searches, whether pagination added
recent work, whether native Web counter-search found DeepXiv misses, and whether every
important Web discovery was retained and source-verified. This is a Researcher self-check;
the fresh Completion Checker judges only retained state and the structured landscape.

## Resume from authoritative state

When resuming, ignore conversational memory as authority. Recover from:

1. `view` for the current lifecycle, contract, revision, gaps, and landscape;
2. `inspect` for exact objects behind stable references;
3. targeted source reads when evidence must be rechecked;
4. `audit-history` for prior search queries, pagination, filters, and external attempts.

Raw Web results are not recoverable state. Do not repeat searches blindly, but rerun a
needed Web counter-search after resume when a frontier gap remains unresolved.

## Request independent completion

When the Research Contract appears satisfied, call `request-completion`. Completion is a
feedback boundary, not a loop counter: a CONTINUE verdict names concrete blocking gaps
that the Researcher resolves by returning to the loop, and a PASS authorizes Delivery.
There is no forced number of research iterations before completion is allowed, and a
CONTINUE does not reset a counter — it returns specific repair work to the loop.

Then create a fresh checker context that has not participated in the research loop and
follow [COMPLETION_GUIDE.md](references/COMPLETION_GUIDE.md).

The fresh Completion Checker may only:

- call `completion-view`;
- call `completion-inspect` for exact retained objects;
- call `completion-read-source` for targeted evidence verification;
- submit PASS, CONTINUE, or UNCERTAIN.

It must not search, retain papers, mutate research objects, or inherit the Researcher's
private reasoning. It must not use WebSearch or broad Web discovery. CONTINUE must
identify concrete blocking gaps; control then returns to Research. UNCERTAIN is used
when available evidence cannot justify either PASS or a specific repair plan. PASS alone
authorizes complete Delivery.

## Deliver a report

In DELIVERY, build the report from a fresh `delivery-view` and targeted inspections.
Load the two authority documents separately:

```text
c:/Users/wushuhong/Desktop/literature-research-clean-e2e-20260810-195219/.claude/skills/literature-research/references/REPORT_WRITING_GUIDE.md
c:/Users/wushuhong/Desktop/literature-research-clean-e2e-20260810-195219/.claude/skills/literature-research/references/RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_GUIDE.md
```

Apply the complete Writing Guide to the Narrative Planner, Report Composer, Editorial
Integrator, fresh Editor, and Reviser. It governs organization, prose, synthesis, and
readability. Create the independent Research Integrity Reviewer in a fresh context with
the complete Integrity Guide, Delivery state, manuscript, and targeted inspection/source
access. The Integrity Guide is its primary rubric; it does not receive the Writing Guide
as a style rubric and does not perform prose polish.

The semantic stages are:

```text
Narrative Planner
→ Report Composer
→ Editorial Integrator
→ Fresh Editor
→ Reviser when needed
→ Research Integrity Reviewer
→ deterministic citation renderer
→ publish-report
→ validate-delivery
→ close-run
```

If integrity review finds a Delivery-only writing or citation repair, revise in Delivery.
If it finds an unsupported claim or missing research, call `reopen-research` and return
to the research loop.

The fresh Editor reviews the whole report semantically: sections must be driven by
research questions or judgments rather than paper order; taxonomy must state its
classification criterion; each paragraph should make one main judgment and start with
a self-contained claim; giant paragraphs, abstract-noun chains, bureaucratic or
translated prose should be repaired. Representative methods must serve synthesis,
carry the required first-use hyperlink, and lead naturally from evidence to gaps. These
are editorial judgments, not Python paragraph-length or style validators.

The fresh Integrity Reviewer checks author claims versus independent evidence,
single-paper evidence versus consensus, correlation versus causation, ablation versus
causal mechanism, numerical gains versus statistical significance, SOTA and
generalization scope, benchmark validity, robustness and efficiency dimensions,
test-time compute/tool budgets, comparison fairness, recency and absolute claims,
corpus-bounded absence, and citation-to-claim alignment. It returns the existing typed
integrity result without a numeric score.

Integrity may inspect Delivery state and retained objects, reread targeted sources, and
review the manuscript. It must not search broadly, retain papers, mutate Research state,
create Findings, or silently add evidence. Completion asks whether Research State
satisfies the Contract; Integrity asks whether the report faithfully represents that
accepted State. Keep these authority boundaries separate.

When a retained primary paper has a canonical URL, hyperlink the first formal occurrence
of its method or system name to that URL. This navigation link never replaces a structured
citation. Keep citations close to the technical judgments they support.

Paragraph rhythm, natural Chinese, terminology, title density, and appropriate table use
are semantic editorial criteria. Do not ask the Harness to encode them as structural
validators. Preserve experimental conditions and qualifications while improving prose.

Use `render-report` to resolve structured citation tokens deterministically, then pass
the rendered content to `publish-report`. Only close after `validate-delivery` succeeds.

## Wiki orchestration after closure

After a run closes COMPLETE, project accepted cross-run knowledge into the Wiki. The
Wiki is a rebuildable, non-authoritative Markdown projection of CLOSED+COMPLETE runs,
not a run artifact and not a second research runtime: it never enters the lifecycle, is
not a required artifact, and its failure never breaks a closed run or invalidates the
report. Only CLOSED+COMPLETE runs are eligible; partial runs are excluded.

Call `wiki-projection` to read the current authoritative projection of eligible runs.
The projection carries `source_runs` — the `(run_id, state_revision)` identity of every
eligible run at projection time. Preserve it. Synthesize Wiki pages from that projection
— pages that synthesize accepted approaches, findings, and open problems across runs,
each carrying contributing refs to real research entities. Perform the semantic review
of those pages yourself, against the same projection; this is a Claude-side semantic act,
not a harness command field.

Then call `publish-wiki` with `source_runs` (preserved from the projection) and the
reviewed `pages`. Python validates structure and provenance deterministically and
publishes a versioned local build, recording `source_runs` verbatim in the manifest as
honest build provenance. A published Wiki may become stale if a newer run closes COMPLETE
afterwards; that is allowed — the manifest honestly records which run revisions produced
it. Detect staleness with `is_current()` (or by re-projecting and comparing) and rebuild
when desired. There is no publish-time exact-current rejection: a stale `source_runs` is
published, not refused.

Invalid structure or provenance raises `WikiBuildError` before publication, preserving
any previous Wiki. A rejected semantic review is your decision — do not call `publish-wiki`
until the review passes. Either way the run remains CLOSED COMPLETE and the report remains
valid. See `RUNTIME_API.md` for the input shape.

## DeepXiv credential setup

The DeepXiv credential is a user-level install setting, not part of any
ResearchRun. If `doctor` reports that the DeepXiv credential is missing, ask
the user to run:

```text
python "<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/harness.py" configure-token
```

The command stores the token at:

```text
~/.literature-research/deepxiv-token
```

Do not ask the user to modify shell profiles, registry settings, `.env` files,
workspace files, or Skill files. The Harness reads that file back when
`DEEPXIV_TOKEN` is not already in the process environment, so the DeepXiv
providers need no changes. An explicit `DEEPXIV_TOKEN` environment variable
always takes precedence and is never overwritten. Af

# Completion Guide

Completion is an independent verification boundary. The checker must be freshly created
after `request-completion` and must not inherit the Researcher's hidden chain of thought,
scratch material, or conversational confidence.

## Allowed evidence actions

The checker may only use:

- `completion-view` for the complete contract-facing projection;
- `completion-inspect` for exact retained objects behind stable references;
- `completion-read-source` for targeted verification of primary evidence;
- `submit-completion` to record one verdict.

It must not search, retain papers, add or edit analyses, create findings, resolve gaps,
write the report, or modify persistence. If new work is needed, return CONTINUE with
blocking gaps so a Researcher can perform it.

The checker may challenge current knowledge, but does not repair it. It evaluates the
knowledge and evidence exposed through its completion capabilities; it does not audit
the Researcher's search procedure.

## Evaluation criteria

Evaluate the current contract revision, not an earlier version. Check all of the
following:

1. Each requirement is addressed by explicit structured research state.
2. Major technical routes within scope are represented and meaningfully distinguished.
3. Important claims have retained-paper provenance and suitable evidence locators.
4. Representative methods have been inspected deeply enough to support mechanism-level
   comparisons, not merely named from search results. A PaperAnalysis derived only
   from abstract or search/discovery metadata does not satisfy this criterion: it is
   a blocking deficiency, not a borderline case. If a representative paper carries
   detailed `key_results`, `contributions`, or `limitations` but has no corresponding
   `inspect-source`/`read-source` grounding, return CONTINUE with a blocking gap
   naming that paper and the missing primary-source evidence.
5. Experimental results preserve model, task, baseline, hardware, or other material
   conditions needed to interpret them.
6. Contradictory or non-comparable evidence is not flattened into a false consensus.
7. Limitations and unresolved questions that affect the deliverable are explicit.
8. Open Investigation Gaps do not block a contract requirement.
9. For latest/current/recent requests, the retained corpus and structured landscape
   demonstrate reasonable frontier coverage. Recent primary work supports the relevant
   route, trend, comparison, or open-problem claims, and the evidence is recent enough
   for the Contract's stated time-sensitive scope.
10. The landscape can support the promised deliverable without inventing new research
    during report writing.

Do not demand a fixed number of papers. A mature narrow topic may need fewer sources than
a broad fragmented field. Conversely, a large hit count does not establish coverage.

An empty `key_locators` tuple or a null `LiteratureSource.locator` is not by itself a
failure. Locators are required where one meaningfully exists for the cited claim; their
absence is a signal to inspect the paper and confirm the grounding, not an automatic
block. The block is the missing primary-source evidence behind a detailed claim, not
the empty field.

## Verdicts

### PASS

Use PASS only when every contract requirement is adequately supported, remaining limits
are compatible with the deliverable, and no open gap blocks completion. Reasons should
summarize why the evidence is sufficient and note accepted boundaries.

### CONTINUE

Use CONTINUE when specific research work can repair the deficiency. Include one or more
blocking gap specifications that say what evidence or synthesis is missing and connect it
to affected requirement or approach references when possible. Do not prescribe a fixed
query; describe the knowledge deficit.

Examples include a missing major route, inadequate primary-source evidence, absent
frontier coverage, unresolved contradiction, or a representative paper whose
PaperAnalysis records detailed mechanism-level or empirical claims but rests only on
its abstract or search metadata rather than inspected primary source. The last case is
a P0 signal: name the paper and the missing primary-source grounding in the blocking
gap. A representative paper that has not been analyzed beyond its abstract is also a
blocking case when the contract requires mechanism-level understanding.

### UNCERTAIN

Use UNCERTAIN when the available state does not justify PASS, but the checker also cannot
form a defensible concrete repair plan. Explain the uncertainty. UNCERTAIN returns control
to Research without manufacturing blocking gaps.

## Submission discipline

Submit exactly one verdict for the pending CompletionCheck and current state revision.
PASS and UNCERTAIN must not contain blocking-gap payloads. CONTINUE must contain at least
one valid new or reopened blocking gap. Once submitted, the request metadata and completed
verdict are immutable facts.

content.content:
1	# Report Writing Guide
2	
3	本指南定义 AI / ML 技术调研与 DeepResearch 报告的长期写作标准。
4	
5	Research State 决定报告**可以陈述什么**；本指南规定这些研究结果**如何组织和表达**。它不保存研究事实，不判断研究是否完成，也不替代 Research Integrity Review。
6	
7	目标是把已经完成的研究组织成：
8	
9	> **面向专业读者的现代研究报告：概念正式，句法自然；结论先行，证据跟随；判断明确，语气克制。**
10	
11	最终文本应像熟悉该领域的研究员在完成充分阅读和比较之后，对当前问题、方法关系、证据边界和未知部分做出的清晰说明。
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. 从研究问题组织报告
16	
17	报告不是 Paper、Approach Family、Finding 或 Open Problem 的可视化转储。
18	
19	正文优先围绕读者真正需要回答的问题组织，例如：
20	
21	* 不同方法究竟在改变哪个技术变量；
22	* 同一路线内部的方法差异在哪里；
23	* 某项收益来自机制本身还是额外计算预算；
24	* 不同论文为什么得出不同结果；
25	* 当前证据能支持什么，不能支持什么。
26	
27	标题应让读者知道：
28	
29	> 这一节要解决什么问题，或者这一节已经得到什么关键判断。
30	
31	避免只有主题名称的标题，也不要为了吸引注意而写成媒体式标题。
32	
33	例如，与其写：
34	
35	> KV Cache Quantization
36	
37	更适合写：
38	
39	> KV Cache 量化降低了存储成本，但低比特误差仍受异常值影响
40	
41	或者：
42	
43	> KV Cache 量化如何在压缩率和生成质量之间取舍？
44	
45	具体使用问题式还是判断式标题，由文章整体结构决定。
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 2. Synthesis 优先于 Summary
50	
51	调研报告的价值主要来自论文之间的关系，而不是摘要数量。
52	
53	避免：
54	
55	> Paper A 提出……
56	>
57	> Paper B 提出……
58	>
59	> Paper C 在此基础上……
60	
61	优先说明：
62	
63	* 多篇工作解决的是不是同一个问题；
64	* 它们的核心机制有什么不同；
65	* 哪些结果能够互相支持；
66	* 哪些结果因为实验条件不同不能直接比较；
67	* 后续工作究竟改变了什么；
68	* 当前证据还缺什么。
69	
70	一个实用判断是：
71	
72	> **如果删除论文名称后，一段文字就失去了组织结构，它很可能仍然是论文列表，而不是 synthesis。**
73	
74	论文名称应该出现在真正需要识别代表方法、历史节点或证据来源的位置，而不是成为正文默认骨架。
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 3. 方法分类必须说明判别标准
79	
80	技术路线分类必须帮助理解，而不是增加标签。
81	
82	不要只写：
83	
84	> 现有方法可以分为 A、B、C、D。
85	
86	应先说明：
87	
88	> 为什么按照这个变量分类？
89	
90	好的分类依据通常能够解释：
91	
92	* 方法机制为什么不同；
93	* 成本来自哪里；
94	* trade-off 为什么不同；
95	* 哪些方法可以组合；
96	* 为什么实验结果可能不同。
97	
98	例如，可以按照“缓存成本通过什么方式被减少”分类，而不是按照不同论文自行使用的模块名称分类。
99	
100	分类是报告为了比较而建立的分析工具，不应写成领域存在天然、严格的若干“流派”。
101	
102	当边界模糊时，应明确说明方法可能跨越多个类别。
103	
104	---
105	
106	## 4. 长报告先建立阅读模型
107	
108	对于领域级 DeepResearch 报告，正文开始时应让“熟悉 AI、但不是该子方向专家”的读者获得最小可用模型。
109	
110	通常需要回答：
111	
112	1. 原有方法如何工作；
113	2. 当前瓶颈是什么；
114	3. 新方法改变了哪个假设或决策；
115	4. 因此出现了哪些主要技术路线；
116	5. 后续正文为什么按这些问题展开。
117	
118	不要一开始介绍：
119	
120	* 搜索了多少篇论文；
121	* 执行了多少轮检索；
122	* Agent 如何构建 State；
123	* 内部 coverage 或 confidence。
124	
125	除非用户明确要求 methodology / audit trail，否则报告讨论领域，不讨论 DeepResearch 流程。
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 5. 执行摘要是可选的，不是固定模板
130	
131	对于较长、信息密度较高的领域报告，可以在正文前增加简短执行摘要。
132	
133	执行摘要应由**判断**组成，而不是目录式概括。
134	
135	弱：
136	
137	> 方法分类
138	>
139	> 实验结果
140	>
141	> 未来方向
142	
143	更好：
144	
145	> **量化路线能够直接降低 KV 存储量，但极低比特下的异常值仍是主要质量约束。**
146	
147	> **缓存删除方法节省显存的代价是放弃部分历史状态，其有效性高度依赖 token importance 的稳定性。**
148	
149	> **不同论文的吞吐和延迟结果普遍缺少统一硬件与并发设置，无法据此形成严格路线排序。**
150	
151	执行摘要是否采用列表、自然段以及具体长度，由报告复杂度决定，不机械规定条数。
152	
153	---
154	
155	## 6. 一个段落只完成一个主要论证任务
156	
157	段落是报告最重要的阅读单位。
158	
159	一个段落通常只承担一个主要判断，例如：
160	
161	* 解释机制；
162	* 比较方法；
163	* 给出实验结果；
164	* 分析限制；
165	* 解释证据冲突；
166	* 推导一个 open problem。
167	
168	如果机制、代表方法、实验结果、限制和跨方法比较同时需要展开，应优先拆成相邻自然段。
169	
170	不要把整个小节压缩成一个高密度长段。
171	
172	同时避免另一极端：一句一段、连续短句和过多空行会让报告碎片化。
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 7. 段落默认结构：判断 → 证据 → 限制 → 含义
177	
178	不是每一段都必须机械包含四步，但这是优先使用的论证顺序。
179	
180	### 判断
181	
182	第一句尽量让读者立即知道本段要表达什么。
183	
184	好的首句：
185	
186	> KV Cache eviction 的主要收益来自减少需要长期保留的 token 状态，而不是降低单个 KV 元素的表示成本。
187	
188	弱首句：
189	
190	> 另一方面，这一方向也得到了较多研究关注。
191	
192	### 证据
193	
194	随后给出：
195	
196	* 代表方法；
197	* 具体实验；
198	* 数字；
199	* 多篇论文的共同观察。
200	
201	### 限制
202	
203	说明这个结论在哪些条件下成立，以及哪些比较并不公平。
204	
205	### 含义
206	
207	最后解释：
208	
209	> 这些证据对路线选择、方法关系或当前研究边界意味着什么。
210	
211	不要连续多句不断加强结论，却没有增加新的证据。
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 8. 每段第一句尽量可以独立理解
216	
217	读者快速浏览长报告时，往往首先读取：
218	
219	* 标题；
220	* 每段第一句；
221	* 表格；
222	* 加粗判断。
223	
224	因此段首应尽量包含实际信息，而不是过渡语。
225	
226	避免：
227	
228	* 值得注意的是……
229	* 在此基础上……
230	* 从这一角度来看……
231	* 与此同时……
232	* 此外，相关研究也……
233	
234	优先直接写新的判断。
235	
236	---
237	
238	## 9. 长句只承担真正不可拆分的逻辑
239	
240	技术内容复杂不等于句子必须复杂。
241	
242	如果一个句子同时承担：
243	
244	* 背景；
245	* 方法机制；
246	* 实验数字；
247	* 限定条件；
248	* 推论；
249	
250	应拆成多句。
251	
252	逻辑关系应通过准确的语序和连接表达，而不是依靠大量从句制造“正式感”。
253	
254	短句可以专业。
255	
256	例如：
257	
258	> 更多检索未必带来更好结果。
259	
260	> 现有实验无法直接比较这两条路线。
261	
262	> 论文没有报告端到端 latency。
263	
264	这些表达不需要进一步复杂化。
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 10. 使用现代研究汉语
269	
270	目标是：
271	
272	> **概念正式，句法自然。**
273	
274	普通动作使用自然中文。
275	
276	避免：
277	
278	> 通过 dynamic evidence acquisition 实现 knowledge gap closure。
279	
280	优先：
281	
282	> 系统根据当前证据缺口继续检索，直到关键条件得到覆盖。
283	
284	正式模型名、算法名、标准、缩写和领域内稳定使用的英文术语可以保留。
285	
286	首次出现时可以采用：
287	
288	> 中文解释（English Term）
289	
290	如果中文翻译反而增加歧义，直接保留原术语。
291	
292	同一概念在全文中保持稳定称呼。
293	
294	---
295	
296	## 11. 避免三类典型 AI 文风
297	
298	### 过度口语
299	
300	避免高频使用：
301	
302	* 说白了；
303	* 其实；
304	* 简单来说；
305	* 真正的问题是；
306	* 最关键的是。
307	
308	自然不等于聊天。
309	
310	### 公文腔
311	
312	减少：
313	
314	* 本报告围绕；
315	* 聚焦于；
316	* 基于系统梳理；
317	* 在此基础上；
318	* 全面分析；
319	* 具有重要意义；
320	* 提供有力支撑；
321	* 赋能；
322	* 助力。
323	
324	### 英文论文直译腔
325	
326	减少：
327	
328	* 值得注意的是；
329	* 突显了……的重要性；
330	* 提供了新的视角；
331	* 从这一角度来看；
332	* 这些发现表明；
333	* 不仅……而且……；
334	* 并非简单的……而是……。
335	
336	如果一个事实重要，直接写它为什么重要。
337	
338	---
339	
340	## 12. 控制抽象名词密度
341	
342	以下词不是禁用：
343	
344	* 系统性
345	* 维度
346	* 范式
347	* 框架
348	* 机制
349	* 路径
350	* 视角
351	* 层面
352	* 体系
353	* 能力
354	* 闭环
355	* 方法论
356	
357	但连续堆叠会使文本失去具体含义。
358	
359	判断方法：
360	
361	> 如果删除这些词后，句子的信息几乎没有变化，就优先删除。
362	
363	例如：
364	
365	弱：
366	
367	> 当前在搜索决策机制的系统性建模与动态自适应优化能力维度上仍存在不足。
368	
369	更好：
370	
371	> 现有方法尚不能根据推理过程中的证据变化实时调整搜索决策。
372	
373	---
374	
375	## 13. 比较应围绕真正有意义的维度
376	
377	方法比较不是把所有论文数字放入一张表。
378	
379	应优先比较真正影响选择的问题，例如：
380	
381	* 改变了什么；
382	* 需要什么额外训练；
383	* 推理时增加什么成本；
384	* memory / latency / throughput 的收益来自哪里；
385	* 质量损失在哪里发生；
386	* 对硬件和部署条件有什么依赖；
387	* 是否能够与其他路线组合。
388	
389	如果不同论文的 benchmark、模型、预算和硬件无法对齐，应在正文中说明“不构成严格横向比较”。
390	
391	表格适合多个对象在多个相同维度上的比较。
392	
393	表后只解释最有价值的差异，不逐格复述。
394	
395	---
396	
397	## 14. 证据冲突应解释，而不是贴“争议”标签
398	
399	不同论文结果不同，不自动等于领域存在争议。
400	
401	报告应先判断：
402	
403	* 是否真的检验了同一个命题；
404	* benchmark 是否相同；
405	* 模型是否相同；
406	* 训练和 inference budget 是否相同；
407	* metric 是否相同；
408	* 数据和工具条件是否相同。
409	
410	如果条件不同，应写：
411	
412	> 现有结果并不一致，但目前尚不能判断差异来自方法本身还是实验条件。
413	
414	只有存在真正可比的正反证据时，才更适合使用“冲突”或“争议”。
415	
416	---
417	
418	## 15. 区分不同类型的证据不足
419	
420	不要把所有不确定性统称为“研究空白”。
421	
422	至少区分：
423	
424	**已有冲突**
425	存在方向相反、且具有一定可比性的直接证据。
426	
427	**单边证据**
428	目前主要只有支持一种结论的工作，缺少独立复现或反例。
429	
430	**不可比较**
431	有多个方法，但实验条件差异太大，无法形成可靠排序。
432	
433	**证据不足**
434	论文提出了某项结论，但实验设计只能支持更弱的说法。
435	
436	**领域尚未解决**
437	当前文献确实没有解决某个重要问题。
438	
439	Research Gap 应由前文已有证据自然推出，而不是在结尾临时添加“未来可以进一步研究”。
440	
441	---
442	
443	## 16. Report 中不要泄漏内部 Research Runtime
444	
445	正文默认不出现：
446	
447	* ApproachFamily；
448	* LandscapeFinding；
449	* InvestigationGap；
450	* CompletionCheck；
451	* coverage score；
452	* confidence score；
453	* internal refs；
454	* agent iteration；
455	* search round history。
456	
457	这些可以帮助 Research Runtime 工作，但不是领域事实。
458	
459	如果用户需要方法学附录或 audit trail，可以单独输出。
460	
461	---
462	
463	## 17. 方法名称优先提供 Primary Paper 导航
464	
465	当算法、系统或方法拥有当前 retained Paper 中明确的 canonical URL 时：
466	
467	第一次正式介绍该方法名称，应优先写成 Markdown 超链接：
468	
469	```markdown
470	[MethodName](canonical-paper-url)
471	```
472	
473	例如：
474	
475	```markdown
476	[SnapKV](https://arxiv.org/abs/...)
477	```
478	
479	超链接的作用是方便读者进入 Primary Paper。
480	
481	它**不替代正式 citation**。
482	
483	相关机制、实验数字和判断仍应使用结构化引用，并尽量靠近实际 claim。
484	
485	同一方法后续出现时不必重复链接。
486	
487	---
488	
489	## 18. 引用应落在实际证据位置
490	
491	一个 citation 不应无差别地支撑整段多个不同命题。
492	
493	如果一段同时包含：
494	
495	* 方法事实；
496	* 数字结果；
497	* 机制解释；
498	* 报告自身综合判断；
499	
500	应尽量让不同证据各自靠近对应表述。
501	
502	尤其注意：
503	
504	> Paper introduction 中的 motivation 不等于实验已经验证的事实。
505	
506	> Author claim 不等于独立复现。
507	
508	> Abstract 的概括不能自动替代具体实验 setting。
509	
510	---
511	
512	## 19. 数字用于提高可验证性
513	
514	在数字能够帮助读者判断时，优先给出具体变化，而不是抽象评价。
515	
516	优先：
517	
518	> 平均搜索轮次由 5.8 降至 3.9，但论文未报告端到端 latency。
519	
520	而不是：
521	
522	> 搜索效率明显提高。
523	
524	数字必须保留必要条件，例如：
525	
526	* benchmark；
527	* model；
528	* baseline；
529	* hardware；
530	* batch size；
531	* budget。
532	
533	不要为了显得精确而加入与结论无关的数字。
534	
535	---
536	
537	## 20. 时效性表述必须有边界
538	
539	对于：
540	
541	* 当前；
542	* 最新；
543	* 目前；
544	* 尚无工作；
545	* 首次；
546	* 唯一；
547	* 主流；
548	* SOTA；
549	
550	等时间敏感表述，应结合当前 Research Run 的检索截止日期和 scope。
551	
552	优先：
553	
554	> 截至本次检索截止日，在当前纳入的公开文献中……
555	
556	而不是：
557	
558	> 目前没有任何工作……
559	
560	具体日期来自当前研究过程，不写死在本 Guide 中。
561	
562	---
563	
564	## 21. Fresh Editor 进行整篇文章编辑
565	
566	最终编辑不是逐句润色，而是重新检查文章结构。
567	
568	Fresh Editor 应重点判断：
569	
570	* 主线是否清楚；
571	* 每一节是否回答真实研究问题；
572	* 是否仍有论文逐篇罗列；
573	* taxonomy 是否有判别依据；
574	* 是否存在重复解释；
575	* 是否有超长高密度段落；
576	* 每段首句是否承载实际判断；
577	* 是否有无意义过渡句；
578	* 标题是否只有主题名称；
579	* 比较维度是否公平、清楚；
580	* gap 是否由前文推出；
581	* 是否存在公文腔、翻译腔、抽象名词链；
582	* 是否保留所有重要限定条件。
583	
584	Editor 可以：
585	
586	* 移动；
587	* 合并；
588	* 拆分；
589	* 删除；
590	* 重写段落。
591	
592	但不能创造 Research State 中不存在的新事实或实质研究判断。
593	
594	发现事实边界问题时，应交给 Research Integrity Review，而不是通过写作技巧掩盖。
595	
596	---
597	
598	## 22. 最终目标
599	
600	交付前确认：
601	
602	* 报告回答的是用户问题，而不是复述 Research State；
603	* 章节按研究问题和判断组织；
604	* 方法关系比论文顺序更突出；
605	* 重要路线具有真实 synthesis；
606	* taxonomy 有明确依据；
607	* 每段通常只有一个主要判断；
608	* 段首能够帮助快速阅读；
609	* 关键证据和限制靠近结论；
610	* 专业术语准确，但普通句法自然；
611	* 没有明显 DeepResearch 流程泄漏；
612	* 方法名称具备合理的 Primary Paper 导航；
613	* 报告可以被专业读者快速浏览，也经得起逐条核查。
614	
615	最终目标是：
616	
617	> **用最少但足够的信息，让读者准确理解一个领域的问题、主要方法、方法关系、证据强弱、当前分歧和未知边界。**

# Report Writing Guide

本指南定义 AI / ML 技术调研与 DeepResearch 报告的长期写作标准。

Research State 决定报告**可以陈述什么**；本指南规定这些研究结果**如何组织和表达**。它不保存研究事实，不判断研究是否完成，也不替代 Research Integrity Review。

目标是把已经完成的研究组织成：

> **面向专业读者的现代研究报告：概念正式，句法自然；结论先行，证据跟随；判断明确，语气克制。**

最终文本应像熟悉该领域的研究员在完成充分阅读和比较之后，对当前问题、方法关系、证据边界和未知部分做出的清晰说明。

---

## 1. 从研究问题组织报告

报告不是 Paper、Approach Family、Finding 或 Open Problem 的可视化转储。

正文优先围绕读者真正需要回答的问题组织，例如：

* 不同方法究竟在改变哪个技术变量；
* 同一路线内部的方法差异在哪里；
* 某项收益来自机制本身还是额外计算预算；
* 不同论文为什么得出不同结果；
* 当前证据能支持什么，不能支持什么。

标题应让读者知道：

> 这一节要解决什么问题，或者这一节已经得到什么关键判断。

避免只有主题名称的标题，也不要为了吸引注意而写成媒体式标题。

例如，与其写：

> KV Cache Quantization

更适合写：

> KV Cache 量化降低了存储成本，但低比特误差仍受异常值影响

或者：

> KV Cache 量化如何在压缩率和生成质量之间取舍？

具体使用问题式还是判断式标题，由文章整体结构决定。

---

## 2. Synthesis 优先于 Summary

调研报告的价值主要来自论文之间的关系，而不是摘要数量。

避免：

> Paper A 提出……
>
> Paper B 提出……
>
> Paper C 在此基础上……

优先说明：

* 多篇工作解决的是不是同一个问题；
* 它们的核心机制有什么不同；
* 哪些结果能够互相支持；
* 哪些结果因为实验条件不同不能直接比较；
* 后续工作究竟改变了什么；
* 当前证据还缺什么。

一个实用判断是：

> **如果删除论文名称后，一段文字就失去了组织结构，它很可能仍然是论文列表，而不是 synthesis。**

论文名称应该出现在真正需要识别代表方法、历史节点或证据来源的位置，而不是成为正文默认骨架。

---

## 3. 方法分类必须说明判别标准

技术路线分类必须帮助理解，而不是增加标签。

不要只写：

> 现有方法可以分为 A、B、C、D。

应先说明：

> 为什么按照这个变量分类？

好的分类依据通常能够解释：

* 方法机制为什么不同；
* 成本来自哪里；
* trade-off 为什么不同；
* 哪些方法可以组合；
* 为什么实验结果可能不同。

例如，可以按照“缓存成本通过什么方式被减少”分类，而不是按照不同论文自行使用的模块名称分类。

分类是报告为了比较而建立的分析工具，不应写成领域存在天然、严格的若干“流派”。

当边界模糊时，应明确说明方法可能跨越多个类别。

---

## 4. 长报告先建立阅读模型

对于领域级 DeepResearch 报告，正文开始时应让“熟悉 AI、但不是该子方向专家”的读者获得最小可用模型。

通常需要回答：

1. 原有方法如何工作；
2. 当前瓶颈是什么；
3. 新方法改变了哪个假设或决策；
4. 因此出现了哪些主要技术路线；
5. 后续正文为什么按这些问题展开。

不要一开始介绍：

* 搜索了多少篇论文；
* 执行了多少轮检索；
* Agent 如何构建 State；
* 内部 coverage 或 confidence。

除非用户明确要求 methodology / audit trail，否则报告讨论领域，不讨论 DeepResearch 流程。

---

## 5. 执行摘要是可选的，不是固定模板

对于较长、信息密度较高的领域报告，可以在正文前增加简短执行摘要。

执行摘要应由**判断**组成，而不是目录式概括。

弱：

> 方法分类
>
> 实验结果
>
> 未来方向

更好：

> **量化路线能够直接降低 KV 存储量，但极低比特下的异常值仍是主要质量约束。**

> **缓存删除方法节省显存的代价是放弃部分历史状态，其有效性高度依赖 token importance 的稳定性。**

> **不同论文的吞吐和延迟结果普遍缺少统一硬件与并发设置，无法据此形成严格路线排序。**

执行摘要是否采用列表、自然段以及具体长度，由报告复杂度决定，不机械规定条数。

---

## 6. 一个段落只完成一个主要论证任务

段落是报告最重要的阅读单位。

一个段落通常只承担一个主要判断，例如：

* 解释机制；
* 比较方法；
* 给出实验结果；
* 分析限制；
* 解释证据冲突；
* 推导一个 open problem。

如果机制、代表方法、实验结果、限制和跨方法比较同时需要展开，应优先拆成相邻自然段。

不要把整个小节压缩成一个高密度长段。

同时避免另一极端：一句一段、连续短句和过多空行会让报告碎片化。

---

## 7. 段落默认结构：判断 → 证据 → 限制 → 含义

不是每一段都必须机械包含四步，但这是优先使用的论证顺序。

### 判断

第一句尽量让读者立即知道本段要表达什么。

好的首句：

> KV Cache eviction 的主要收益来自减少需要长期保留的 token 状态，而不是降低单个 KV 元素的表示成本。

弱首句：

> 另一方面，这一方向也得到了较多研究关注。

### 证据

随后给出：

* 代表方法；
* 具体实验；
* 数字；
* 多篇论文的共同观察。

### 限制

说明这个结论在哪些条件下成立，以及哪些比较并不公平。

### 含义

最后解释：

> 这些证据对路线选择、方法关系或当前研究边界意味着什么。

不要连续多句不断加强结论，却没有增加新的证据。

---

## 8. 每段第一句尽量可以独立理解

读者快速浏览长报告时，往往首先读取：

* 标题；
* 每段第一句；
* 表格；
* 加粗判断。

因此段首应尽量包含实际信息，而不是过渡语。

避免：

* 值得注意的是……
* 在此基础上……
* 从这一角度来看……
* 与此同时……
* 此外，相关研究也……

优先直接写新的判断。

---

## 9. 长句只承担真正不可拆分的逻辑

技术内容复杂不等于句子必须复杂。

如果一个句子同时承担：

* 背景；
* 方法机制；
* 实验数字；
* 限定条件；
* 推论；

应拆成多句。

逻辑关系应通过准确的语序和连接表达，而不是依靠大量从句制造“正式感”。

短句可以专业。

例如：

> 更多检索未必带来更好结果。

> 现有实验无法直接比较这两条路线。

> 论文没有报告端到端 latency。

这些表达不需要进一步复杂化。

---

## 10. 使用现代研究汉语

目标是：

> **概念正式，句法自然。**

普通动作使用自然中文。

避免：

> 通过 dynamic evidence acquisition 实现 knowledge gap closure。

优先：

> 系统根据当前证据缺口继续检索，直到关键条件得到覆盖。

正式模型名、算法名、标准、缩写和领域内稳定使用的英文术语可以保留。

首次出现时可以采用：

> 中文解释（English Term）

如果中文翻译反而增加歧义，直接保留原术语。

同一概念在全文中保持稳定称呼。

---

## 11. 避免三类典型 AI 文风

### 过度口语

避免高频使用：

* 说白了；
* 其实；
* 简单来说；
* 真正的问题是；
* 最关键的是。

自然不等于聊天。

### 公文腔

减少：

* 本报告围绕；
* 聚焦于；
* 基于系统梳理；
* 在此基础上；
* 全面分析；
* 具有重要意义；
* 提供有力支撑；
* 赋能；
* 助力。

### 英文论文直译腔

减少：

* 值得注意的是；
* 突显了……的重要性；
* 提供了新的视角；
* 从这一角度来看；
* 这些发现表明；
* 不仅……而且……；
* 并非简单的……而是……。

如果一个事实重要，直接写它为什么重要。

---

## 12. 控制抽象名词密度

以下词不是禁用：

* 系统性
* 维度
* 范式
* 框架
* 机制
* 路径
* 视角
* 层面
* 体系
* 能力
* 闭环
* 方法论

但连续堆叠会使文本失去具体含义。

判断方法：

> 如果删除这些词后，句子的信息几乎没有变化，就优先删除。

例如：

弱：

> 当前在搜索决策机制的系统性建模与动态自适应优化能力维度上仍存在不足。

更好：

> 现有方法尚不能根据推理过程中的证据变化实时调整搜索决策。

---

## 13. 比较应围绕真正有意义的维度

方法比较不是把所有论文数字放入一张表。

应优先比较真正影响选择的问题，例如：

* 改变了什么；
* 需要什么额外训练；
* 推理时增加什么成本；
* memory / latency / throughput 的收益来自哪里；
* 质量损失在哪里发生；
* 对硬件和部署条件有什么依赖；
* 是否能够与其他路线组合。

如果不同论文的 benchmark、模型、预算和硬件无法对齐，应在正文中说明“不构成严格横向比较”。

表格适合多个对象在多个相同维度上的比较。

表后只解释最有价值的差异，不逐格复述。

---

## 14. 证据冲突应解释，而不是贴“争议”标签

不同论文结果不同，不自动等于领域存在争议。

报告应先判断：

* 是否真的检验了同一个命题；
* benchmark 是否相同；
* 模型是否相同；
* 训练和 inference budget 是否相同；
* metric 是否相同；
* 数据和工具条件是否相同。

如果条件不同，应写：

> 现有结果并不一致，但目前尚不能判断差异来自方法本身还是实验条件。

只有存在真正可比的正反证据时，才更适合使用“冲突”或“争议”。

---

## 15. 区分不同类型的证据不足

不要把所有不确定性统称为“研究空白”。

至少区分：

**已有冲突**
存在方向相反、且具有一定可比性的直接证据。

**单边证据**
目前主要只有支持一种结论的工作，缺少独立复现或反例。

**不可比较**
有多个方法，但实验条件差异太大，无法形成可靠排序。

**证据不足**
论文提出了某项结论，但实验设计只能支持更弱的说法。

**领域尚未解决**
当前文献确实没有解决某个重要问题。

Research Gap 应由前文已有证据自然推出，而不是在结尾临时添加“未来可以进一步研究”。

---

## 16. Report 中不要泄漏内部 Research Runtime

正文默认不出现：

* ApproachFamily；
* LandscapeFinding；
* InvestigationGap；
* CompletionCheck；
* coverage score；
* confidence score；
* internal refs；
* agent iteration；
* search round history。

这些可以帮助 Research Runtime 工作，但不是领域事实。

如果用户需要方法学附录或 audit trail，可以单独输出。

---

## 17. 方法名称优先提供 Primary Paper 导航

当算法、系统或方法拥有当前 retained Paper 中明确的 canonical URL 时：

第一次正式介绍该方法名称，应优先写成 Markdown 超链接：

```markdown
[MethodName](canonical-paper-url)
```

例如：

```markdown
[SnapKV](https://arxiv.org/abs/...)
```

超链接的作用是方便读者进入 Primary Paper。

它**不替代正式 citation**。

相关机制、实验数字和判断仍应使用结构化引用，并尽量靠近实际 claim。

同一方法后续出现时不必重复链接。

---

## 18. 引用应落在实际证据位置

一个 citation 不应无差别地支撑整段多个不同命题。

如果一段同时包含：

* 方法事实；
* 数字结果；
* 机制解释；
* 报告自身综合判断；

应尽量让不同证据各自靠近对应表述。

尤其注意：

> Paper introduction 中的 motivation 不等于实验已经验证的事实。

> Author claim 不等于独立复现。

> Abstract 的概括不能自动替代具体实验 setting。

---

## 19. 数字用于提高可验证性

在数字能够帮助读者判断时，优先给出具体变化，而不是抽象评价。

优先：

> 平均搜索轮次由 5.8 降至 3.9，但论文未报告端到端 latency。

而不是：

> 搜索效率明显提高。

数字必须保留必要条件，例如：

* benchmark；
* model；
* baseline；
* hardware；
* batch size；
* budget。

不要为了显得精确而加入与结论无关的数字。

---

## 20. 时效性表述必须有边界

对于：

* 当前；
* 最新；
* 目前；
* 尚无工作；
* 首次；
* 唯一；
* 主流；
* SOTA；

等时间敏感表述，应结合当前 Research Run 的检索截止日期和 scope。

优先：

> 截至本次检索截止日，在当前纳入的公开文献中……

而不是：

> 目前没有任何工作……

具体日期来自当前研究过程，不写死在本 Guide 中。

---

## 21. Fresh Editor 进行整篇文章编辑

最终编辑不是逐句润色，而是重新检查文章结构。

Fresh Editor 应重点判断：

* 主线是否清楚；
* 每一节是否回答真实研究问题；
* 是否仍有论文逐篇罗列；
* taxonomy 是否有判别依据；
* 是否存在重复解释；
* 是否有超长高密度段落；
* 每段首句是否承载实际判断；
* 是否有无意义过渡句；
* 标题是否只有主题名称；
* 比较维度是否公平、清楚；
* gap 是否由前文推出；
* 是否存在公文腔、翻译腔、抽象名词链；
* 是否保留所有重要限定条件。

Editor 可以：

* 移动；
* 合并；
* 拆分；
* 删除；
* 重写段落。

但不能创造 Research State 中不存在的新事实或实质研究判断。

发现事实边界问题时，应交给 Research Integrity Review，而不是通过写作技巧掩盖。

---

## 22. 最终目标

交付前确认：

* 报告回答的是用户问题，而不是复述 Research State；
* 章节按研究问题和判断组织；
* 方法关系比论文顺序更突出；
* 重要路线具有真实 synthesis；
* taxonomy 有明确依据；
* 每段通常只有一个主要判断；
* 段首能够帮助快速阅读；
* 关键证据和限制靠近结论；
* 专业术语准确，但普通句法自然；
* 没有明显 DeepResearch 流程泄漏；
* 方法名称具备合理的 Primary Paper 导航；
* 报告可以被专业读者快速浏览，也经得起逐条核查。

最终目标是：

> **用最少但足够的信息，让读者准确理解一个领域的问题、主要方法、方法关系、证据强弱、当前分歧和未知边界。**

7	它只回答一个问题：
8	
9	> **当前报告中的每个重要判断，其强度是否与 Research State 和 Primary Evidence 的强度匹配？**
10	
11	Research Integrity Reviewer 可以要求修改 Delivery，也可以在发现实质研究缺口时要求返回 Research。
12	
13	不得通过“润色”补齐不存在的证据。
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. 基本原则
18	
19	报告不得：
20	
21	* 新增 Research State 中不存在的实质结论；
22	* 把相关性改写成因果关系；
23	* 把单篇论文结果扩大为领域共识；
24	* 把作者自述改写成独立验证事实；
25	* 把有限 benchmark 结果推广成一般能力；
26	* 删除会改变技术含义的实验条件；
27	* 隐去重要负面结果；
28	* 用更强语气替换不确定结论。
29	
30	如果证据只能支持弱判断，应降低表述强度。
31	
32	如果报告需要的新判断本身有价值但当前 State 没有证据，应：
33	
34	> 返回 Research，而不是让 Writer 自行补充。
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. 区分证据层级
39	
40	至少区分：
41	
42	### 作者报告
43	
44	> 作者报告该方法在指定实验中优于其比较基线。
45	
46	### 独立复现
47	
48	> 后续独立工作在相似条件下复现了该趋势。
49	
50	### 多篇一致证据
51	
52	> 多篇相互独立研究在可比较条件下观察到类似结果。
53	
54	只有第三类才更接近领域层面的稳定结论。
55	
56	如果实际上只有一篇论文，应写：
57	
58	> 该论文的实验显示……
59	
60	而不是：
61	
62	> 研究表明……
63	
64	### 摘要与 discovery metadata 不是 Primary Evidence
65	
66	报告中的机制级判断、实证结果与详细比较，必须来自 `inspect-source` / `read-source`
67	获得的一手原文，而不是 abstract 或搜索元数据。如果 State 中的 PaperAnalysis 仅基于
68	摘要，Integrity Reviewer 应将其视为证据不足，要求返回 Research 补充一手证据，而非
69	通过润色强化表述。详见 RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md 的 Primary Evidence Gate。
70	
71	---
72	
73	## 3. SOTA 是高风险表述
74	
75	“SOTA”必须有明确范围。
76	
77	至少检查：
78	
79	* benchmark；
80	* split；
81	* metric；
82	* model / method category；
83	* comparison set；
84	* 时间范围。
85	
86	避免：
87	
88	> 该方法达到 SOTA。
89	
90	优先：
91	
92	> 在作者报告的 X benchmark、Y split 和 Z metric 上，该方法高于论文列出的同期基线。
93	
94	如果不同工作使用不同：
95	
96	* backbone；
97	* prompt；
98	* tool budget；
99	* context length；
100	* retrieval corpus；
101	* sampling 次数；
102	
103	则不能仅根据最高分判断方法机制更优。
104	
105	---
106	
107	## 4. 数值提升不等于统计显著
108	
109	如果论文没有统计显著性检验，不使用：
110	
111	> 显著提升
112	
113	来表示 numerically higher。
114	
115	优先：
116	
117	> 指标由 71.4 提高至 73.7。
118	
119	或：
120	
121	> 提高 2.3 个百分点。
122	
123	只有明确报告 statistical significance 时，才使用：
124	
125	> 统计显著
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 5. 经验结果通常不构成“证明”
130	
131	对于经验论文：
132	
133	避免：
134	
135	> 实验证明 reflection 提升推理能力。
136	
137	优先：
138	
139	> 在作者测试的模型和任务上，引入 reflection 后准确率提高。
140	
141	“证明”主要适用于：
142	
143	* formal theorem；
144	* mathematical proof；
145	* 明确的形式化正确性结论。
146	
147	---
148	
149	## 6. 泛化必须说明泛化到哪里
150	
151	不要因为多个 benchmark 都提高，就写：
152	
153	> 具有良好泛化能力。
154	
155	应区分：
156	
157	* in-domain；
158	* cross-dataset；
159	* cross-task；
160	* cross-model；
161	* OOD；
162	* temporal；
163	* tool/environment transfer。
164	
165	报告必须明确实际验证的是哪一种。
166	
167	---
168	
169	## 7. 鲁棒性必须说明扰动维度
170	
171	“鲁棒”没有独立含义。
172	
173	需要明确对什么变化鲁棒，例如：
174	
175	* prompt variation；
176	* retrieval noise；
177	* adversarial perturbation；
178	* model variation；
179	* tool failure；
180	* long-context noise；
181	* incomplete observation；
182	* distribution shift。
183	
184	优先：
185	
186	> 在加入一定比例无关检索结果后，该方法性能下降幅度小于 baseline。
187	
188	而不是：
189	
190	> 方法具有较强鲁棒性。
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 8. 效率必须说明是哪一种成本
195	
196	“更高效”可能指：
197	
198	* latency；
199	* throughput；
200	* FLOPs；
201	* token usage；
202	* model calls；
203	* search rounds；
204	* tool calls；
205	* memory；
206	* GPU hours；
207	* dollar cost。
208	
209	报告只能对论文实际测量的维度作判断。
210	
211	例如：
212	
213	> 该方法减少平均搜索轮次，但论文未报告端到端 latency，因此不能判断实际运行时间是否更短。
214	
215	不要用一个“效率”概括多个未测量维度。
216	
217	---
218	
219	## 9. Test-time compute 和工具预算必须显式考虑
220	
221	Agent、DeepResearch、reasoning、multi-agent 方法尤其需要检查：
222	
223	* input tokens；
224	* output tokens；
225	* reasoning tokens；
226	* sampling 次数；
227	* retrieval calls；
228	* browser/tool calls；
229	* model calls；
230	* wall-clock latency；
231	* parallelism。
232	
233	如果性能提升伴随明显更高 inference budget，报告必须说明。
234	
235	不能自动把收益归因于方法机制。
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 10. 可扩展性必须说明尺度变量
240	
241	不要因为“更大模型上也有效”就写：
242	
243	> scalable
244	
245	可扩展性可能针对：
246	
247	* model size；
248	* dataset size；
249	* context length；
250	* number of agents；
251	* tool count；
252	* task horizon；
253	* corpus size；
254	* concurrency；
255	* training cost。
256	
257	必须写清论文实际验证了哪个尺度。
258	
259	---
260	
261	## 11. Benchmark 表现不等于一般能力
262	
263	Benchmark 是特定任务分布和评测协议。
264	
265	例如：
266	
267	> 在 BrowseComp 上提高 10%
268	
269	只能直接说明：
270	
271	> 方法在 BrowseComp 所定义的任务和评测协议下得到更高分数。
272	
273	不能直接推出：
274	
275	> DeepResearch 能力提高 10%。
276	
277	检查 benchmark 是否真实覆盖报告声称的能力。
278	
279	---
280	
281	## 12. 不同 benchmark 分数不能横向排序
282	
283	即使两个 benchmark 都是百分制，也不能写：
284	
285	> A 在 X 得 70，B 在 Y 得 75，所以 B 更强。
286	
287	不同任务、metric 和评测协议之间没有天然可比性。
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 13. LLM-as-a-Judge 需要单独限定
292	
293	如果结果依赖 LLM judge，检查是否报告：
294	
295	* judge model；
296	* rubric；
297	* pointwise / pairwise；
298	* 是否 blind；
299	* 是否有人类一致性验证；
300	* judge 是否可能偏向某类输出。
301	
302	不要把 judge score 写成无条件客观指标。
303	
304	---
305	
306	## 14. 方法比较必须考虑公平性
307	
308	跨论文比较时至少检查：
309	
310	* backbone；
311	* model size；
312	* training data；
313	* retrieval corpus；
314	* context window；
315	* sample count；
316	* inference budget；
317	* tool access；
318	* search API；
319	* maximum steps；
320	* prompt；
321	* proprietary model；
322	* baseline 来源；
323	* extra supervision；
324	* test-time training；
325	* hardware。
326	
327	如果关键条件不同，应明确：
328	
329	> 这些结果只能说明各方法在各自实验设置下的表现，不能构成严格的横向排序。
330	
331	---
332	
333	## 15. Ablation 不自动证明机制
334	
335	例如：
336	
337	> 去掉 verifier 后性能下降。
338	
339	可以支持：
340	
341	> verifier 对完整系统性能有贡献。
342	
343	不能自动支持：
344	
345	> verifier 通过提高证据充分性判断准确率而提升性能。
346	
347	应区分：
348	
349	* component necessity；
350	* component contribution；
351	* causal mechanism；
352	* explanatory hypothesis。
353	
354	作者对机制的解释如果没有独立证据，应保持为解释或假设。
355	
356	---
357	
358	## 16. 冲突必须确认双方真的可比较
359	
360	不要因为 A 与 B 的结果不同就写：
361	
362	> 领域存在争议。
363	
364	先检查：
365	
366	* base model；
367	* task；
368	* budget；
369	* metric；
370	* prompt；
371	* training regime；
372	* data contamination；
373	* evaluation protocol。
374	
375	如果这些不同，更准确的是：
376	
377	> 现有结果并不一致，但尚不能判断差异来自方法还是实验条件。
378	
379	---
380	
381	## 17. Research Gap 必须由已有证据推出
382	
383	高质量 gap 应满足：
384	
385	1. 已说明已有方法；
386	2. 已说明这些方法解决了什么；
387	3. 已说明它们共同没有解决什么；
388	4. gap 与前文 evidence 有直接关系。
389	
390	避免：
391	
392	> 未来可以探索更智能、更动态、更高效的方法。
393	
394	如果没有当前 corpus 支撑，不应把想象中的新方向写成“领域空白”。
395	
396	---
397	
398	## 18. 区分不同的不确定性
399	
400	报告应区分：
401	
402	### 已有冲突
403	
404	存在方向相反且可比较的证据。
405	
406	### 单边证据
407	
408	目前只有一侧结果，缺少独立复现或反例。
409	
410	### 不可比较
411	
412	论文很多，但 benchmark、模型或 budget 差异导致无法排序。
413	
414	### 证据不足
415	
416	论文进行了相关实验，但不足以支持它自己或报告中的强结论。
417	
418	### Corpus-bounded absence
419	
420	本次检索范围中没有找到直接证据。
421	
422	最后一种不能写成：
423	
424	> 没有任何工作研究……
425	
426	应限定：
427	
428	> 截至本次检索截止日，在当前纳入和检索到的公开文献中，尚未发现……
429	
430	---
431	
432	## 19. 时间敏感和绝对表述必须特别审查
433	
434	高风险词包括：
435	
436	* 首次；
437	* 唯一；
438	* 全部；
439	* 所有；
440	* 没有任何；
441	* 从未；
442	* 当前 SOTA；
443	* 主流；
444	* 普遍；
445	* 一致认为；
446	* 已形成共识；
447	* 完全解决；
448	* 根本原因；
449	* 必然。
450	
451	这些表述必须有足够 evidence 和 scope。
452	
453	优先增加边界：
454	
455	> 在作者比较的 baseline 范围内……
456	
457	> 在本次纳入的文献中……
458	
459	> 在该 benchmark 和模型设置下……
460	
461	> 截至本次检索截止日……
462	
463	不要把 Corpus Search History 本身当 proof；它只能帮助限定 absence claim 的范围。
464	
465	---
466	
467	## 20. 数字必须对应实际证据
468	
469	报告中的关键数字应能追溯到：
470	
471	* retained Paper；
472	  -具体 locator；
473	  -具体 experiment / table / figure；
474	  -对应模型和任务设置。
475	
476	不能：
477	
478	* 从 abstract 推导更详细数字；
479	* 合并不同实验 setting；
480	* 对不同论文结果直接平均；
481	* 把相对提升和百分点混用；
482	* 忽略 baseline。
483	
484	---
485	
486	## 21. Citation 与 claim 应一一匹配
487	
488	Integrity Reviewer 应检查：
489	
490	> 这个 citation 实际支持前面的哪一句？
491	
492	一个 citation 不应被用于覆盖一段中的多个不同事实。
493	
494	特别检查：
495	
496	* motivation ≠ evidence；
497	* introduction claim ≠ verified result；
498	* author interpretation ≠ causal proof；
499	* provider summary ≠ Primary Evidence；
500	* search snippet ≠ Research State。
501	
502	---
503	
504	## 22. Report 推断必须与 State 区分
505	
506	报告可以进行 synthesis，但不能创造新的 substantive research knowledge。
507	
508	允许：
509	
510	> 根据 State 中已有多篇论文关系，重新组织并表达一个已经存在的综合判断。
511	
512	不允许：
513	
514	> Writer 在阅读 Delivery View 后自行产生 State 中从未形成的新领域结论。
515	
516	如果新的 synthesis 实际构成重要研究判断：
517	
518	> 返回 Research，形成正式 Finding，再继续 Delivery。
519	
520	---
521	
522	## 23. Integrity Reviewer 的处理方式
523	
524	发现问题后分两类。
525	
526	### Delivery-only repair
527	
528	例如：
529	
530	* 语气过强；
531	* citation 放置错误；
532	* 数字表述错误；
533	* scope 限定遗漏；
534	* 把 author claim 写成共识。
535	
536	可以在 Delivery 中修正。
537	
538	### Research deficiency
539	
540	例如：
541	
542	* 缺少支撑关键结论的 Primary Paper；
543	* 路线之间需要新的实质比较；
544	* 某项重要冲突尚未验证；
545	* 最新发展没有进入 State；
546	* 新的 Open Problem 需要额外证据。
547	
548	必须：
549	
550	> REOPEN_RESEARCH
551	
552	Integrity Reviewer 不自行 broad search，不自行补 PaperAnalysis，不直接修改 Landscape。
553	
554	---
555	
556	## 24. 最终检查
557	
558	交付前重点确认：
559	
560	* 单篇论文没有被写成领域共识；
561	* author claim 与独立证据有明确区别；
562	* correlation 没有升级为 causation；
563	* ablation 没有升级为机制证明；
564	* benchmark 结果没有升级为一般能力；
565	* SOTA、显著、泛化、鲁棒、效率、scalable 都有明确范围；
566	* 方法比较考虑了 backbone、budget 和评测差异；
567	* 额外 test-time compute 被如实说明；
568	* absolute / time-sensitive claim 有 scope；
569	* 重要数字和 citation 可追溯；
570	* corpus-bounded absence 没有被写成 universal absence；
571	* 报告没有创造 Research State 之外的实质结论。
572	
573	最终原则：
574	
575	> **判断可以明确，但判断强度必须与证据强度一致。**
576
